approaches.name: Safe zones for pin placement in the pediatric distal tibia and fibula
aliases: child distal tibia external fixator pin safe zones
approaches.corridor: Mini-open pin corridors in the distal tibia placed at least 2 cm proximal to the physis, directed anteromedial to posterolateral, avoiding the anterior tibial vessels and the peroneal bundle

sources.title: Safe zones for pin placement (pediatric distal tibia and fibula)

procedure_applications.condition: A pediatric distal tibial fracture is stabilized with smooth wires or an external fixator

positioning.text: Position supine with the leg on a radiolucent support and imaging available to locate the distal tibial physis.

surface_landmarks.text: Identify the distal tibial physis and the anteromedial subcutaneous surface of the distal tibia; plan pins at least 2 cm proximal to the physis.

incision.text: Make a 1 cm incision with dissection down to bone for each pin rather than inserting percutaneously.

superficial_interval.text: Spread to bone under direct vision, protecting the extensor tendons and neurovascular structures with small retractors.

deep_interval.text: Direct pins anteromedial to posterolateral, or medial to anterolateral as a secondary route, staying at least 2 cm proximal to the physis.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, extensor tendons and anterior neurovascular bundle, and the distal tibial metaphyseal cortex.

structures_at_risk.text: The distal tibial physis, the anterior tibial artery and vein anteriorly, and the peroneal bundle near the posterolateral tibial border are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Percutaneous insertion in the distal tibia is dangerous, and a posterolateral direction endangers the peroneal neurovascular bundle, so both are avoided.

retraction_hazards.text: Use small retractors to protect the anterior neurovascular bundle and extensor tendons and avoid levering against the physis.

exposure.text: Provides safe mini-open corridors for smooth wires or external fixator pins in the pediatric distal tibia.

limitations.text: Pin placement is constrained by the physis proximally and the anterior and peroneal neurovascular structures, leaving a narrow safe corridor.

indications.text: Indicated for smooth wire or external fixator pin placement in the pediatric distal tibia and fibula.

closure.text: Close each mini-incision loosely around the pin to avoid skin tension.

complications.text: Complications include growth disturbance from physeal injury, anterior tibial or peroneal neurovascular injury, and pin-tract problems.

questions.question: How far proximal to the physis should pediatric distal tibial pins be placed?
questions.answer: At least 2 cm proximal to the physis.

questions.question: Which direction of pin insertion is avoided and why?
questions.answer: The posterolateral direction, because it endangers the peroneal neurovascular bundle.

questions.question: Why is a 1 cm incision used instead of percutaneous pinning here?
questions.answer: Because percutaneous insertion in the distal tibia is dangerous to the neurovascular structures.
